fit.summary: Four years in a medical ICU with vents, drips, and precepting, plus med-surg charge experience; no cardiac surgery patients and no CCRN.

bullets.text: Charge nurse 1 shift a week; helped cut falls with injury from 9 to 3 in a year with bed alarms and purposeful rounding

cover_letter.hook: Summit Valley Health's cardiovascular ICU is the next step I have been working toward from a medical ICU, and night shift suits me.
cover_letter.body:
At Lakeshore Regional Medical Center I care for 2 critically ill patients per shift in a 24-bed medical ICU, including ventilated patients and continuous drips. I joined our sepsis workgroup, which raised on-time bundle completion from 68% to 91% in one year, and I have precepted 7 new graduate nurses through their 12-week orientation.

I started on a 32-bed medical-surgical unit at Prairie View Hospital, where I worked as charge nurse 1 shift a week. I chart in Epic and hold an active Wisconsin RN license with current BLS and ACLS.
cover_letter.close: I would like to hear how your unit supports nurses moving from a medical ICU to cardiac surgery patients.

gaps: CCRN is preferred; Daniel has not sat the exam.
